instructions: At least 4 hours ahead, or the night before: grate 6 of the garlic cloves into a large bowl. Add 3/4 cup of the yogurt, 3 tbsp of the olive oil, the juice of 1 lemon, the 1 1/2 tbsp tomato paste, the 1 1/2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp allspice, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp ginger, 1/2 tsp oregano, 1/4 tsp nutmeg, 1/2 tsp pepper and 1 1/2 tsp of the salt. Whisk until smooth.
Cut the 2 lb chicken into 1 1/2 inch cubes, add them to the bowl and turn them until every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate.
Put 8 wooden skewers in a dish of water to soak for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the upper third. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and brush it with the last 1 tbsp olive oil.
Cut the bell pepper and the onion into 1 1/2 inch pieces and sprinkle them with 1/4 tsp of the salt.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers with a piece of pepper or onion between every couple of cubes. Leave a little space between the pieces. Lay the skewers on the sheet.

Roast for 10 minutes. Turn the skewers over and roast for another 6 to 8 minutes. If you're grilling instead, cook them over medium high for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until charred in spots.

Switch the oven to broil and broil the skewers for 2 to 3 minutes, until the edges char in spots. Watch them closely. You're cooking the chicken to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when there's no pink left.
Meanwhile, stir the last 1/2 cup yogurt with the last garlic clove, grated, the juice of half the second lemon and the last 1/4 tsp salt. Cut the other half of the lemon into wedges.
Move the skewers to a plate and cover them loosely with foil. Let them rest for 5 minutes.
While they rest, wrap the pitas in foil and put them in the oven, turned off, for 5 minutes to warm. Chop a small handful of the parsley and scatter it over the skewers.
Taste a piece of chicken. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt first, then a squeeze from one of the lemon wedges.
Serve with the garlic yogurt, the warm pita and the lemon wedges.
advance_prep_notes: Marinate the chicken at least 4 hours ahead, or the night before.
method_notes: All three marinate cubed chicken in yogurt, lemon, olive oil, plenty of garlic and tomato paste, then thread it onto skewers and cook it hot. Simply Lebanese uses breast, a warm tawook blend of paprika, allspice, cinnamon, ginger, oregano, white pepper and nutmeg, marinates 1 to 4 hours and grills it for 10 to 15 minutes, serving it with toum and pita. An Edible Mosaic uses thighs with paprika, allspice and cayenne and lets them marinate up to 24 hours; Munaty Cooking threads bell pepper onto the skewers, sears them in a pan and rests them under foil. This one follows Simply Lebanese's marinade, adds Munaty's pepper and onion, roasts the skewers hot and finishes them under the broiler, with a quick garlic yogurt standing in for toum. Thighs work too and stay juicier; cook them to 175°F.
